## Context
When a record reaches the loop with no comment marker, board_advance.asks emits an advance ask without requested_at, and test_an_undated_ask_carries_no_stamp_rather_than_this_instant pins that. The board snapshot schema requires requested_at on every ask, so basicly board exits 3 and test_mode_a_writes_the_page_and_the_contract_beside_it fails on the live ledger. It turned main CI red on e203ce77 after the lane C merge put basicly-9cv5p17 in intake; closing that record cleared the symptom only. Date the ask from the record's own last ledger event of any kind, not only comment markers.
payload.title: Date every advance ask so the board snapshot stays valid

Options must price a bound on the joined wait: a joined claim not pushed within N seconds leaves the join and pushes itself, with N taken from the data. payload.text: Orchestrator decision 2026-11-12: the floor run was stopped at 14:04 UTC as contaminated. Partial data, labelled contaminated: 104 claims and 94 pushes in 9.5 min; git work per claim with zero added latency was mean 0.11 s, p99 0.47 s, max 0.59 s. So the simulated push and fetch latency explains almost all of the 6.42 s p99 git work in the design-rate run. The floor run is needed only if the quiet gate run fails. The FOREIGN_CPU_LIMIT of 0.03 is accepted as a start; recheck it against the quiet baseline and record the measured number beside it. The decisive run: design rate, seed 1, 30 minutes, cpu_foreign reported, in the window Handily Implementation names; it counts if cpu_foreign is under the limit. Whatever the gate shows, the joined-wait bound is owed. If the gate passes, it is the first step of .43.16, with the burst as its proof test: 52 sessions all claiming in the first minute, every claim answered within 30 s, no exit 4.

Quiet window agreed with Handily Implementation 2026-11-12: 14:30 to 15:05 UTC. In it, handily runs no test suite, commit gate, live tmux check, install gate or plugin test, and its release waits. Basicly runs nothing else on this machine in that window. Plan: a 30 s quiet baseline at 14:30, then the decisive run (design rate, seed 1, 30 min, cpu_foreign reported).

Orchestrator hold 2026-11-12: the owner corrected the requirements. The tracker must work with any git, must not depend on GitHub as a provider or on the gh CLI, must be present and bother no one, and carry no setup overhead. His case is 3 to 9 people on one repository, about 200 pull requests a day with AI, and not everyone may push to main. A separate vault repository, a registry and a claim protocol are too heavy. Stopped until the orchestrator sends the outcome: .43.16, .43.17, .43.20, S2c (.43.8, .43.9), S7, the joined-wait bound and any new vault task. No new design by this session. Continues: main green, and small non-vault defect fixes. The quiet gate run in the agreed window 14:30 to 15:05 UTC still runs.

Quiet gate run 2026-11-12, 14:30:30 to 15:00:30 UTC, in the window agreed with Handily: PASS. 52 sessions, 13 machines, scale 1, seed 1, 30 min, design rate 8.85 claims per session per hour. 278 claims; exits 0: 224, 3: 54; no record with two holders; no session without a claim. p50 2.78 s, p95 6.30 s, p99 8.38 s, max 9.20 s. Per claim p99: process start 0.10 s, share lock 0.01 s, fetch lock 0.60 s, joined wait 1.21 s, claim inside the process 8.31 s, git work 6.25 s, push retries 2. Busiest minute 20 pushes, mean 9.43 per minute. cpu_foreign mean 0.01, p99 0.03, max 0.10, under the 0.03 limit. Quiet baseline at 14:30 was mean 0.004, max 0.006. Overlap: this session's own commit hooks ran until 14:37 inside the window, which likely made the 0.10 max sample. The limit stays 0.03, about 7 times the quiet baseline. Known open: the burst case (joined wait p99 29 s, two exits of 4) is untouched by this result.

Orchestrator decision 2026-11-12: the quiet run counts, and the design-rate gate is PASSED at p99 8.38 s. Reasons: foreign mean 0.01 is under the 0.03 limit; foreign load can only slow a claim, and the run passed with it. The margin is 1.62 s, so no second seed is needed. Proof that the earlier failures were load: the same seed 1 under foreign load gave p99 10.12 s. .43.18 stays open for the burst finding (joined wait p99 29 s, two exits of 4) and under the hold on new vault slices until the owner answers the concept question.

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the climb ends, the report shall give a grade table of every candidate on P1 to P10, the winner, the strongest argument against it, what the owner must decide or reverse, what of today's code stays, and an estimate to a usable tracker, with every number marked measured, sourced or assumed.
payload.description:
## Context
When the owner corrected the tracker requirements on 2026-11-12 (any git host, no provider or gh, nothing to set up, a flat file count, no push rights on main, 3 to 9 people with about 200 pull requests a day), I want to grade four storage shapes against those properties in a short hill-climb, so the owner can pick a winner before more vault work is built. Candidates: A vault repository as built, B a dedicated tracker branch with the same per-writer files and claim code, C events that travel with the work branches, D a server such as Dolt. Time box 2 hours, at most 2 rounds, no product code; a spike in a scratch folder is allowed.
payload.title: Pick a tracker storage shape for the corrected owner requirements

payload.text: Brief from the orchestrator for the owner, 2026-11-12. Fixed properties, graded 0 to 10: P1 git only, any host, no provider API or gh. P2 setup: commands, repositories, tokens and chores a team needs; zero is the target. P3 file count stays flat with pull requests, branches, records and events; 200 pull requests a day is 2,000 in 10 days. P4 no pull request ever conflicts on tracker data. P5 no push rights on main needed. P6 load: 3 to 9 people, about 200 pull requests a day with AI. P7 a claim is known within seconds; no record with two holders. P8 in sync with the code. P9 nothing hidden: ordinary tools show the data, and a person can find and remove it. P10 clone size and noise on the code repository after one year. Tie-breaker only: how much of today's built code stays. Candidates: A vault repository in its best form (one command, registry optional); B one dedicated tracker branch with per-writer files and the built share and claim code (the owner banned an orphan branch on 2026-11-11 under nothing hidden; grade P9 on what each host shows); C events travel with the work branches, reads fold main plus every remote branch, branch name is the claim, a routine pull request compacts (grade with and without compaction); D a server such as Dolt. At most one candidate E if a grader finds a shape that beats these on P2 and P3 together. Method: hill-climb with fresh graders per round, at most 2 rounds, only the top two improve between rounds, a fresh verifier runs falsify-first and one spike on the leader; for B the spike runs the built share and claim code on a branch of a local bare repository, runs T-share-smoke and the claim proofs, and measures repository size after one simulated year and what a default and a single-branch clone fetch; interface-facts for GitHub and Bitbucket on CI for a branch with no pipeline file and branch rules that exempt one branch. A council votes if two candidates end within one grade point. Time box 2 hours, no product code.

Climb result 2026-11-12, 2 rounds, 8 graders, 1 verifier with a spike, council of 3. Round 1 sums of lowest grades: A 69, B 59, C 57, C+ 58, D 59, E 74 (E = B made readable). Round 2: A2 65, E2 59 (means 7.5 and 7.3). Council A2 3 to 0, voted before the verifier reported. Verifier: 'A2 reads from a shallow clone' broke (a depth-1 clone folds 0 holders and a claim from it landed on a held record; the built code never makes a shallow clone, so this blocks a proposed shortcut, not today's code); 'A2 setup is one command' broke (git cannot create a host repository; 5 to 6 host steps plus one invitation per member; no init verb); 'never two holders with full history' held (117 proof tests passed). Full-history cost in the built log format: 1.31 KiB per commit marginal (measured), about 270 MiB per year and about 38 minutes of first fold per year (extrapolated); shared by any shape that uses the built log and fold. Verdict: A, the vault repository in its BUILT log form; v2's state files, generation floor, create-on-init and .git/ local copy are dropped. Not a clean win: E2 beats A2 on P1 (8 against 6) and P2 (7 against 4); A leads on P10 and P5. No candidate meets both the 2026-11-11 rulings as relayed (no tracker branch, git refs banned, the separate backlog repository stands) and the 2026-11-12 correction as relayed (a second repository is too heavy). Owner decisions: (1) keep a second repository with a manual host step, or lift the branch ban and accept that a default code clone carries the tracker history (measured 71 to 491 MiB in one simulated year, on the rejected state-file format); recommend the repository; (2) the claim protocol stays; (3) history growth stands until a checkpoint design exists. D (a server) scored 59 with P1 at 0 to 2. Estimate, assumed: 8 to 12 slices, 2 to 3 weeks, plus 1 to 2 weeks for the unscoped checkpoint design.

payload.acceptance_criteria: When a check that declares itself timed runs under basicly verify, the runner shall report the foreign CPU share of the machine over that check's own window, counting sibling checks as foreign.
payload.description:
## Context
When a consumer project such as handily runs a timed test check inside basicly's pre-commit runner, the runner starts sibling checks in parallel (check_execution.py _run_parallel), so the timed check shares the machine with them and with other projects. Handily measured on 2026-11-12 (handily-5rspdc) that its speed gate refused three commits from load, not slow tests: quiet runs stayed under the limit, loaded runs went over with test-time sums 12 percent higher. I want basicly to give a timed check a measured foreign CPU share over its own window, counting sibling checks as foreign, as claim_load.py does for load runs, so a gate can refuse to count a noisy run instead of failing it.
payload.title: Expose foreign cpu share to a consumer speed gate run beside parallel checks

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the design task ends, the report shall give the split of first-fold cost into fetching, walking and checking commits, and parsing events, the draft in under a page with answers to the five orchestrator questions, the verifier's breaks, the measured first-read time, shallow clone size and history-read time after one simulated year, the effect on the tracker branch candidate, and a recommendation.
payload.description:
## Context
When a new machine first reads the vault, the built fold walks and checks every commit from genesis; the spike for basicly-4z4zte8 extrapolated about 38 minutes and about 270 MiB per year of history at the owner's load. The owner asked on 2026-11-12: 'did you think about archiving? done items do not require to be read, only if explicitly required'. I want one draft design of a checkpoint commit that holds only the open records, so a normal read starts there and closed records are read only on request, with one fresh verifier and one spike, so the owner can choose between a vault repository and a tracker branch. No product code; time box 2 hours.
payload.title: Design a checkpoint that archives closed records out of the normal read

payload.text: Brief from the orchestrator 2026-11-12, from the owner's archiving idea. First answer from measurement what makes the first fold cost about 38 minutes per year: fetching, walking and checking commits, or parsing events. Idea to design and break: (1) a checkpoint commit holds a snapshot of the open records only (fields, holder, open edges); fresh segment files start after it; (2) a normal read starts at the newest checkpoint and never reads history before it; (3) done records stay in git history and are read only on explicit request; (4) a clone may be shallow down to the newest checkpoint and no deeper; the tool refuses a shallower clone; (5) any writer may write a checkpoint past a threshold; two writers race like two claims; (6) a checkpoint is valid only if its snapshot equals the fold of its parent; a full reader or fsck proves it, a shallow reader trusts it. Answer: (a) an event after a checkpoint for an archived record; (b) an open record that depends on a closed one; (c) never two holders across the boundary; (d) whether the snapshot grows without end; (e) the never-events and nothing hidden. Spike one simulated year: normal first read time, shallow clone size, one explicit history read; then what the design does to the tracker branch candidate (a period branch that restarts at a checkpoint). One draft, one fresh verifier, one spike, 2 hours, no product code; the vault hold stays.

Owner decision 2026-11-12, relayed by the orchestrator: (1) the owner agrees to the vault repository design (candidate A as built); the name is open and sets the default repository name at init; the orchestrator recommends 'the vault' with default repository name backlog-vault. (2) Migration must not lose existing backlogs: basicly ledger files (events-*.jsonl, pending-*.jsonl, snapshot.jsonl) and br/beads issues.jsonl or similar JSON or JSONL trackers; ids are kept. (3) Requirements in the owner's words: 'basicly tracker can be installed as standalone and as part of basicly harness'; 'basicly tracker can be used with other harnesses and can hook into them (example with scripts, skills, cli, api, and so on)'; 'we do not need any secrets, tokens or similar' - the vault uses the person's own git credentials; the CI testbed token, the two repository variables and the testbed-probe job are dropped from .43.25. (4) Dogfood cutover approved in order basicly, handily, terminal, each after the one before works (ledger lines measured by the orchestrator: basicly 19150, handily 4194, terminal 2096; all three code repositories public). (5) Open owner question: one vault for many projects or one per project. The hold on vault slices ends; nothing is built before the plan is sent to the orchestrator.

Owner decision 2026-11-12, relayed by the orchestrator: (1) the owner agrees to the vault repository design (candidate A as built); the name is open and sets the default repository name at init; the orchestrator recommends 'the vault' with default repository name backlog-vault. (2) Migration must not lose existing backlogs: basicly ledger files (events-*.jsonl, pending-*.jsonl, snapshot.jsonl) and br/beads issues.jsonl or similar JSON or JSONL trackers; ids are kept. (3) Requirements in the owner's words: 'basicly tracker can be installed as standalone and as part of basicly harness'; 'basicly tracker can be used with other harnesses and can hook into them (example with scripts, skills, cli, api, and so on)'; 'we do not need any secrets, tokens or similar' - the vault uses the person's own git credentials; the CI testbed token, the two repository variables and the testbed-probe job are dropped from .43.25. (4) Dogfood cutover approved in order basicly, handily, terminal, each after the one before works (ledger lines measured by the orchestrator: basicly 19150, handily 4194, terminal 2096; all three code repositories public). (5) Open owner question: one vault for many projects or one per project. The hold on vault slices ends; nothing is built before the plan is sent to the orchestrator.

Owner answers 2026-11-12, relayed by the orchestrator, 'approved': (1) topology: one vault holds one or more projects; the vault is the access boundary; the default is one vault per team; for the owner, one vault for basicly, handily and terminal. (2) Name: 'the vault'; the default repository name at init is backlog-vault. (3) Visibility: private by default. The orchestrator created backlog-vault under the owner's account, private and empty; nothing is pushed to it before the plan is accepted, and the first push is the real init with genesis. basicly-testbed-registry is removed by the owner; basicly-testbed-vault stays as the sandbox for the real-host proof with the owner's own git login until the basicly cutover is proven. No token exists and none will.

Result 2026-11-12. Split of the built first fold (measured, 4,010 commits, 57.7 s): checking commits 97 % (cat-file of old and new segment 67 %, diff-tree 15 %), walking (rev-list per commit) 14 %, local fetch 0.8 %, parsing 0.3 %; 10.8 to 14.4 ms per commit, growing as segments fill. Spike, one full simulated year (250 days, 210,935 commits, 299,254 events, 59 checkpoints every 5,000 events), measured: normal first read 17.7 s at the tip and 22.7 s worst case, against about 38 minutes for a full fold (extrapolated); clone shallow to the newest checkpoint 1.2 to 1.4 MiB; checkpoint.json 74 to 103 KiB, 167 to 234 open records; one explicit history read 8.3 s unshallow (84.6 MiB) plus 7.8 s search, or about 1 s after the fetch using the closed ids in checkpoint messages; whole vault 114 MiB size-pack (generator differs from the baseline, so the drop is not all from checkpoints; checkpoints alone saved about 21 % at 20 days). Tracker branch E with a period branch: 1.36 MiB of tracker objects in a default clone against 97.7 MiB for the full branch, but old periods then live only under a custom ref (refs/tracker-archive/*), which is a git ref outside branches, the hidden storage the owner banned; under a tag they come back into every clone; with no ref they are pruned. Verifier on draft 1: fail with 5 fixable breaks (a depth refetch false retraction and repair replay giving two holders; no create or restore in the fold; built shape rules quarantine a checkpoint and quarantine is a skip; fold_digest separate from the snapshot and no comparer when alone; the depth from commit text is untrusted) and 1 nit. Recommendation: the checkpoint design holds with those fixes; build it after the basicly cutover, as a slice of about 5 hours, plus a 1 to 2 hour batching of git calls in the fold.
